title: GCC Adopts Policy Rejecting Significant AI-Generated Code - Slashdot
excerpt: GCC has adopted a policy rejecting substantial code contributions generated by or derived from LLMs. "This covers not just code copied directly from tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, or GitHub Copilot, but also any versions of the code later edited or rewritten by a human, provided that the final contribu...
content_html:
GCC has adopted a policy rejecting substantial code contributions generated by or derived from LLMs. "This covers not just code copied directly from tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, or GitHub Copilot, but also any versions of the code later edited or rewritten by a human, provided that the final contribution is still based on material generated by the system," reports Linuxiac. From the report: The important point, then, is not whether a developer has used an AI tool at some stage in their work; contributors can use LLMs to discuss ideas, understand existing code, learn about a field they are unfamiliar with, or carry out general research. The limitation lies in the inclusion of copyright-significant material generated by such tools in the code submitted to GCC.

The policy also provides for a few limited exceptions; GCC maintainers are allowed to accept changes that are legally insignificant or trivial and are generated by an LLM, on the condition that they meet the project's normal contribution requirements and the use of an LLM is clearly disclosed.

Furthermore, copyright-significant AI-generated test cases could still be accepted. Since test cases usually involve small programs which are intended to reproduce compiler bugs or to verify certain behavior, the policy deals with them separately from code that is incorporated into GCC itself.

It does not follow that merely looking at or altering the generated code makes it acceptable. By the rules that have been adopted, a contributor cannot take substantial implementation produced by an LLM, clean it up manually, and then treat the resulting patch as if it had been originally written by them. Once a contribution has been derived from generated content, it is still subject to the policy.

sentences.en: GCC has adopted a policy rejecting substantial code contributions generated by or derived from LLMs.

sentences.en: "This covers not just code copied directly from tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, or GitHub Copilot, but also any versions of the code later edited or rewritten by a human, provided that the final contribution is still based on material generated by the system," reports Linuxiac.

sentences.zh: 限制在于提交给 GCC 的代码中包含了此类工具生成的具有版权意义的材料。

sentences.en: The policy also provides for a few limited exceptions; GCC maintainers are allowed to accept changes that are legally insignificant or trivial and are generated by an LLM, on the condition that they meet the project's normal contribution requirements and the use of an LLM is clearly disclosed.
sentences.zh: 该政策还规定了一些有限的例外情况； GCC 维护者可以接受法律上不重要或微不足道的、由 LLM 产生的变更，条件是他们满足项目的正常贡献要求，并且明确披露 LLM 的使用。

sentences.en: Furthermore, copyright-significant AI-generated test cases could still be accepted.
sentences.zh: 此外，具有版权意义的人工智能生成的测试用例仍然可以被接受。

sentences.zh: 由于测试用例通常涉及旨在重现编译器错误或验证某些行为的小程序，因此该策略将它们与合并到 GCC 本身的代码分开处理。

sentences.en: It does not follow that merely looking at or altering the generated code makes it acceptable.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着仅仅查看或更改生成的代码就可以接受。

sentences.en: By the rules that have been adopted, a contributor cannot take substantial implementation produced by an LLM, clean it up manually, and then treat the resulting patch as if it had been originally written by them.
sentences.zh: 根据已采用的规则，贡献者不能采用法学硕士生成的实质性实现，手动清理它，然后将生成的补丁视为他们最初编写的补丁。

sentences.en: Once a contribution has been derived from generated content, it is still subject to the policy.
sentences.zh: 一旦从生成的内容中获得贡献，它仍然受该政策的约束。
